text: I implemented automatic linkification of plain-text URLs in the markdown rendering pipeline, with minimal changes and preserved sanitization. Summary of changes - Location: bookmarks/templatetags/shared.py, function render_markdown - Processing order: 1) Convert markdown to HTML using the existing Markdown renderer. 2) Linkify plain URLs with bleach.linkify, explicitly skipping a, code, and pre tags. 3) Sanitize with bleach.clean using the existing allowlists, ensuring a and href are allowed if not already present. - Added a short comment explaining the order and skip_tags rationale. - No changes to templates, fixtures, translations, or the permanent test suite. Key code snippet - In render_markdown: - as_html = renderer.convert(markdown_text) - linkified_html = bleach.linkify(as_html, skip_tags=['a', 'code', 'pre']) - sanitized_html = bleach.clean(linkified_html, allowed_tags, allowed_attrs) - return mark_safe(sanitized_html) - allowed_tags/allowed_attrs are derived from the existing bleach_allowlist values; a and href are added only if missing, without broadening the policy. Security and behavior - Linkify first, sanitize second preserves the existing security model. Any disallowed attributes (e.g., rel) will be stripped by bleach.clean per the allowlist. - No target or rel attributes were added or altered. - Linkification is skipped inside anchors and code/pre blocks to avoid undesired linkification. Local validation - Created a temporary test bookmarks/tests/test_autolink_tmp.py to verify: - Plain URL becomes clickable: https://example.com. - Inline code and fenced code blocks do not linkify. - Ran targeted tests: - pytest -q -k autolink_tmp: 3 passed. - pytest -q -k bookmarks: all existing tests passed. - Removed the temporary test file before finalization and re-ran pytest -q -k bookmarks to confirm all existing tests still pass. Acceptance criteria met - Plain URLs in notes/description are converted into clickable anchors. - URLs inside inline code or code blocks are not linkified. - Sanitization still applies, preserving the security model. - No permanent changes to tests, templates, or unrelated code. - Changes are minimal and documented with a short comment. If you’d like, I can open a PR with this focused change.
